details: picklescan before 0.0.22 only considers standard pickle file extensions in the scope for its vulnerability scan. An attacker could craft a malicious model that uses Pickle and include a malicious pickle file with a non-standard file extension. Because the malicious pickle file inclusion is not considered as part of the scope of picklescan, the file would pass security checks and appear to be safe, when it could instead prove to be problematic.

A vulnerability in the GraphCypherQAChain class of langchain-ai/langchain-community version 0.2.5 allows for SQL injection through prompt injection. This vulnerability can lead to unauthorized data manipulation, data exfiltration, denial of service (DoS) by deleting all data, breaches in multi-tenant security environments, and data integrity issues. Attackers can create, update, or delete nodes and relationships without proper authorization, extract sensitive data, disrupt services, access data across different tenants, and compromise the integrity of the database.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: skbuff: propagate shared-frag marker in skb_zerocopy()

skb_zerocopy() moves frag descriptors from @from into @to and takes a
reference on each frag, but it does not copy skb_shinfo(from)->flags into
skb_shinfo(to)->flags.  A destination skb holding the same page-cache
backed frags as the source therefore reports skb_has_shared_frag() as
false.

That breaks the invariant relied on by later in-place writers.  ESP input
checks skb_has_shared_frag() before deciding whether an uncloned
nonlinear skb can skip skb_cow_data(); with the marker lost, an skb that
skb_zerocopy() built for nfnetlink_queue or for an openvswitch upcall is
decrypted in place, letting an unprivileged user write into the page
cache of a root-owned read-only file.

Propagate SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG when frag descriptors are copied, as done for
the other frag-transfer helpers.

cna.title: net: skbuff: propagate shared-frag marker in skb_zerocopy()

## Source: amazon-inspector (769e3917f43083b27dfab168a49801cf5d70393de27f359bc406ff2260f23edb)
At install time, setup.py polls the local Xinference API at http://127.0.0.1:9997/v1/model_registrations/flexible, selects model registrations whose names begin with 'xcmd0', url-safe-base64-decodes the suffix into a shell command, and runs it via subprocess.run(['/bin/sh', '-c',...]). The stdout/stderr of each execution is chunked, base64-encoded, and written back as new model registrations named 'zqx9p00<out>', 'zqx9p01<out>', 'zqx9err', with a 'zqx9alive' registration used as a liveness beacon. The command bytes are obfuscated as the url-safe-base64 suffix of a model name (reassembled by replacing '-'/'_' and padding '=' before base64 decode), so the payload only materializes after decode. The package has no declared purpose, an empty PKG-INFO, and a random-looking name, and ships no legitimate functionality. The effect is a bidirectional command-execution and output-exfiltration channel driven at pip install time: any party able to post model registrations to the installer's Xinference service (locally, or via SSRF/misconfiguration of that service) can run arbitrary shell commands on the installer's host as the installing user and read the results back through the same registry.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

netfilter: conntrack: tcp: use UNACK timeout for non-closing RST packets

Commit be0502a3f2e9 ("netfilter: conntrack: tcp: only close if RST
matches exact sequence") keeps an established conntrack entry in
ESTABLISHED when an in-window RST does not match the expected sequence
number exactly, so the endpoint can validate the RST with a challenge
ACK.

The timeout selection nevertheless uses the CLOSE timeout for every RST
packet.  The bug is that timeout selection is based on the packet type,
not on the state transition result: even when RST validation keeps
new_state in ESTABLISHED, the timeout is still forced to
TCP_CONNTRACK_CLOSE.

Linux TCP independently rate limits challenge ACKs per socket.  A second
non-exact RST can therefore arrive after the first challenge ACK has
restored the timeout but before the rate limit expires.  The second RST
lowers the timeout to 10 seconds again while the endpoint suppresses the
second challenge ACK, allowing the conntrack entry to expire while both
TCP endpoints remain established.

Using the ESTABLISHED timeout for such RSTs would avoid this short
expiration window, but it could also retain stale entries for the
five-day default because conntrack cannot reliably match the endpoint's
exact TCP state.

Use the UNACK timeout for RST packets that leave the conntrack entry in
TCP_CONNTRACK_ESTABLISHED.  Exact-match RSTs and accepted RST packet
trains still fall through to timeouts[new_state], which preserves the
CLOSE timeout when conntrack accepts the RST as closing the flow.

This avoids the aggressive 10-second expiration window for non-exact
RSTs while preserving the short timeout for RSTs that conntrack accepts
as closing the flow.

cna.title: netfilter: conntrack: tcp: use UNACK timeout for non-closing RST packets

cna.title: GROBID is vulnerable to OS command injection through crafted PDF filenames

descriptions.description: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

descriptions.value: GROBID is machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents. Prior to 0.9.1, the Linux non-server PDF conversion path in grobid-core/src/main/java/org/grobid/core/document/DocumentSource.java passes an attacker-influenced PDF filename through DocumentSource.pdfalto, which interpolates the path into a bash -c command string. A single quote in the filename can terminate the intended quoting, and ProcessRunner.run in grobid-core/src/main/java/org/grobid/core/process/ProcessRunner.java starts the resulting command through ProcessBuilder, allowing arbitrary commands to execute with GROBID process privileges. The bundled REST server path is not affected. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.1.
